system: You are a careful research assistant.
prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key b60bd4be2305
What the team decided: Stated that violation of the condition does not imply a bad approximation, while satisfaction implies a good one
Restatement: Treat cases where the condition is unmet as inconclusive rather than as bad approximations, since meeting the condition implies a good approximation but failing it does not.
C1: Treat each case where the condition is unmet as inconclusive and measure the actual approximation error empirically in that case rather than counting it as a failure.
C2: Count every case where the condition is unmet as a failure of the approximation there and report the overall fulfillment rate as the quality estimate.

C2: Set the minimum to one class and cap the maximum at a small fixed number chosen once and applied uniformly across the entire benchmark.

=== key 48c20814d34f

Restatement: Prioritize work on detection of scheming over work on prevention when limited resources force a choice between the two, treating detection as the first line of effort.
C1: Prioritize work on detecting scheming first so that any reliance on prevention arguments is backed by an independent way to catch systems that scheme anyway.
C2: Prioritize work on preventing scheming first, directing limited resources toward lowering scheming propensity and blocking scheming actions before harm occurs.

=== key e722485d674c
What the team decided: Use good detection tools, such as detailed far-OOD evals, to validate prevention methods, while avoiding iterating against all detection tools
Restatement: Use good detection tools to validate prevention methods, such as thorough out-of-distribution evals, while avoiding iterating prevention directly against every detection tool.
C1: Prioritize collecting evidence that improves detection of the behavior in naturalistic settings while harms remain low, establishing a measurement basis for later work.
C2: Prioritize evidence that improves prevention of the behavior outright, aiming early effort at methods that stop hidden goal pursuit rather than merely observing it.

C1: Run each model under the fixed simple scaffold and a higher-elicitation scaffold, then fit forecasting curves to the resulting range rather than a single score per model.
C2: Run every model on the fixed simple scaffold with its message and token caps and report those scores consistently as the performance input for the forecasting curves.
